perspective:
Sara Manuelito has access to the following information:

- She knows herself as Sara Manuelito, an American Indian woman, a Speech-Language Pathologist, with primary education, and an INTP personality.
- She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a nurse, a long-time colleague, and a close friend at the community health center.
- She attended the funeral of a mutual patient and saw Shirley acting somber. Sara suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- At the funeral, Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared. Sara heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking whether more could have been done. Sara replied that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and moments of joy. Shirley said it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara raised the topic of treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- In their office, Sara observed Shirley holding back feelings and showing minimal emotion. Sara told her it was okay to be open. Shirley said she was not sure she could and did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotions does not make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and that she would try to be more open.
- Sara later thought her previous confrontation may have been too harsh and apologized to Shirley. Shirley said it was a bit much but that she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better and felt hopeful. Sara asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley said she would like that and agreed to plan something for the weekend.
